accepted_phrases: Autofocus uses sensors, control and a motor to focus a selected point or area, and continuous focus can respond to subjects moving toward or away from the camera. The sports-photography source says interchangeable lenses, fast autofocus, burst rate, reach and wide apertures are commonly important, with indoor sports tending toward shorter and faster lenses because light is dimmer and distances are shorter. Generic descriptions and seller feature claims do not establish tracking accuracy, buffer behavior, flicker performance or keeper rate for any captured model in this gym.

One MachineLearning author asks how ISO, f-number and exposure time affect a dark-condition dataset. One iPhone author reports an oversharpened iPhone 14 Pro sample relative to a Sony A7III and 24-105 f/4. A second iPhone author reports noise, intermittent focus and small files relative to an Android phone. These are scoped questions or self-reports without controlled matching. They justify measuring settings, focus, noise and output rather than assuming all phones or dedicated cameras behave alike.

Shutter speed is exposure time, and shorter exposure admits less light while helping limit motion blur from a moving subject. Lower f-numbers mean larger relative apertures and more entering light. Image noise can arise from sensor and electronic processes, and low-light capture trades exposure time, aperture and gain after their practical limits. Sensor format affects angle of view and can affect total light under matched comparison conditions, but the result is not a one-variable ranking. Stabilization can address camera shake but does not by itself freeze a volleyball player.

The six seller pages are frozen assertions, not current delivered offers or independent performance tests. The Olympus E-M1 page shows SKU B00NGSLTBC at 668 dollars, rated 93 percent over twelve reviews, and calls the offer body only in its title while also displaying style options. The ZS70 bundle page shows SKU B07VNKKKSB at 379.08 dollars, rated 95 percent over four reviews. The LX10 bundle page shows SKU B01NGYHJOQ at 514.87 dollars, rated 80 percent over four reviews. The Canon 80D page shows SKU B01BUYK04A at 798 dollars with no reviews shown and a body-only style. These amounts do not verify tax, shipping, current availability, used condition, exact delivered contents, warranty, return terms, battery health, or a complete under-700-dollar sports system.

The frozen model sources place the Olympus E-M1 introduction in 2013 and identify a 17.3 by 13mm Four Thirds sensor and interchangeable Micro Four Thirds mount. They place the LX10 in 2016 with a fixed 24-72mm-equivalent f/1.4-f/2.8 lens and a 13.2 by 8.8mm sensor, the Canon 80D in 2016 as an interchangeable-lens DSLR, and the ZS70 row in 2017 with a 1/2.3-type sensor, 30x 24-720mm-equivalent f/3.3-f/6.4 lens. This supports exact model, format, lens-form and release mapping only. It does not prove that older is worse, larger is always better, or any model wins in the buyer's gym.

A body-only camera is not a complete volleyball system. The Panasonic 35-100mm f/2.8 page is explicitly a Micro Four Thirds lens at 897.99 dollars and states a 70-200mm-equivalent range. The Sigma 50-100mm f/1.8 page is 999 dollars and explicitly lists compatible Canon APS-C DSLRs including the 80D. These frozen examples show that mount, reach, aperture and lens cost can dominate the body-price comparison. They do not establish that either exact lens is required, currently available, in budget, or independently proven in the gym. Total cost must include the exact compatible lens and required accessories.

Before purchase, verify exact identity, condition, shutter count, battery, mount, compatible lens, aperture through the needed range, reach from the buyer's position, autofocus modes, burst and buffer behavior, card requirements, warranty, return window and complete delivered cost. Rent, borrow, inspect or use a return-compliant trial where allowed. In the same gym, from the same position and for comparable volleyball actions, test declared shutter, aperture and ISO strategies and normalize final output size. Repeat enough bursts to record motion-freeze rate, focus-hit rate, noise and retained detail, keeper rate, handling failures and total system cost separately. Do not use stabilization, one lucky frame or one unblinded favorite as a substitute for these outcomes.

Create one exact-system table that keeps seller assertions, independently mapped model facts, unresolved condition fields, lens compatibility, total delivered cost, field-side outcomes and scope limits in separate columns. Mark every identity, condition, reach, aperture, autofocus, burst, output-quality, handling and budget gate pass, fail or unresolved. Release year, sensor format, megapixels, zoom, store rating and community anecdotes may explain what to test but cannot override a failed or unresolved complete-system gate.

The packet proves no automatic winner. Build a pass, fail, unresolved table for each exact complete system. A candidate may pass only if identity and condition are verified, body and lens are compatible, reach and usable aperture fit the buyer's position, autofocus and burst behavior meet the predeclared same-gym thresholds, noise and detail remain acceptable at the required motion-freezing exposure, handling is workable, and complete delivered cost stays within the declared ceiling. Choose the lowest total-cost passing system. If no option passes or required fields remain unresolved, rent or borrow for a corrected trial, keep using the phone while improving position and settings, save for a complete system, or defer. Report the result only for the tested gym, actions, output size, budget and exact units, not as a universal sensor-size or release-year rule.

The packet proves no automatic camera winner. Choose only the lowest-total-cost exact complete system that passes identity, condition, compatibility, reach, aperture, autofocus, burst, same-gym output, handling and budget gates; otherwise rent, borrow, test, keep the phone, save or defer.

Verify current exact complete systems and compare them in the same gym. Select the lowest-total-cost passing option, or use a reversible fallback when no option passes or required fields remain unresolved.
